analysis.title: Marquee Overlay Issue 036: Oil Expression: The $27 Risk Premium
key_insights: Brent has risen to roughly $112/bbl on escalating Middle East tensions and growing downside risks to supply, which have increased precautionary buying in physical and financial markets.

GS estimates Brent fair value at about $85/bbl, implying a geopolitical risk premium of roughly $27/bbl. Daan Struyven (Commodities Research) assesses that essentially all of the recent rise in crude reflects a higher risk premium, not a higher fair value.
Market-price risks are now increasingly symmetric. The path from here depends on whether supply risks intensify or a durable diplomatic resolution lets the premium unwind.

Brent is steeply backwardated. The forward curve falls from roughly $114/bbl at the front to the high-$80s by late 2027, which points to substantial normalization even as near-term supply risk stays elevated.

Brent has stayed elevated while the Geopolitical Risk Index has retraced from recent spikes. The premium is therefore not only a function of headline geopolitical risk, since precautionary physical buying, supply-chain disruption and financial hedging demand also support prices.
Brent and the US 2Y Treasury yield have both risen materially over the past year and moved sharply higher again through September and October, linking elevated oil to tighter financial conditions.
Preferred expression: hedge geopolitical oil-price upside selectively.

tension_points.bull_case: Supply risks intensify, with precautionary physical buying, supply-chain disruption and hedging demand keeping Brent near $112/bbl and the premium intact.
tension_points.bear_case: A durable diplomatic resolution lets the roughly $27/bbl premium unwind toward GS fair value of about $85/bbl. The backwardated curve already prices substantial normalization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable diplomatic resolution of the Middle East tensions would invalidate the case for holding the premium.
